headline: Tools extended human capabilities—they changed what we could do and who we became
universal_truth: What we create changes us; our tools shape us as much as we shape them
fun_facts: Stone tools date back 3.3 million years—older than our species
The hand evolved partly to grip tools—tools shaped our anatomy
Humans are the only species that makes tools to make other tools
discussion_questions: What tool do you rely on most in daily life?
How have tools changed what humans can accomplish?
What tools are changing you right now?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Without tools, you couldn't cut, cook, build, or travel far. Tools extended what human bodies could do—amplifying our strength, precision, and reach. But tools didn't just change what we could do. They changed who we became.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We think of tools as things we use. But the relationship goes both ways. How did making and using tools change humans ourselves?

options.text: Tool use shaped our hands, brains, and social behavior—we co-evolved with our tools
options.response: Yes. Grip evolved for tool use. Brain regions grew to coordinate tool skills. We are the tool-using ape—shaped by what we made.

options.text: Tools made life easier but didn't change human biology or psychology
options.response: Actually, tool use drove evolutionary changes in hands, brains, and social organization...

q1.title: Older Than Us
q1.script: The oldest stone tools are 3.3 million years old—predating Homo sapiens by millions of years. Our ancestors were tool-makers before they were human. Tools aren't something we invented; they're part of what made us.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Older Than Us"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Tools Making Tools
q2.script: Humans are the only species that makes tools to make other tools. A chimp might use a stick to get termites, but won't sharpen it with a stone. This 'meta-tool' ability—tools for making tools—unlocked unlimited possibility.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Extended Mind
q3.script: Some philosophers argue tools become part of our minds. When you use a pencil, your thoughts extend through it. When you use a computer, it becomes part of your thinking system. We don't just use tools—we merge with them.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What we create changes us. Tools shaped human evolution, and they continue shaping us today. Choose your tools carefully—they're not just things you use, they're things that shape who you become.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 111. Tomorrow, we'll discover the invention of the wheel. Until then, notice the tools you use—and consider how they might be shaping you.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Tool Audit - What's Shaping You?
growTrack.learning_objective: Reflect on how your tools influence you
growTrack.activity: List the five tools you use most—phone, computer, car, whatever. For each, ask: how does this tool change what I can do? How might it be changing how I think or behave? Tools shape users. What are yours shaping?
